original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-kan-base-change}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a Kan fibration of simplicial sets.
Let $Y' \to Y$ be a morphism of simplicial sets.
Then $X \times_Y Y' \to Y'$ is a Kan fibration.

final_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a Kan fibration of simplicial sets.
Let $Y' \to Y$ be a morphism of simplicial sets.
Then $X \times_Y Y' \to Y'$ is a Kan fibration.
hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a Kan fibration of simplicial sets.
Let $Y' \to Y$ be a morphism of simplicial sets.
conclusions: $X \times_Y Y' \to Y'$ is a Kan fibration.

semantic_review_note: Kan fibrations are preserved by simplicial base change to any Y' over Y; source does not require the original f to be trivial or surjective in every degree.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-simplicial-group-kan}
Let $X$ be a simplicial group. Then $X$ is a Kan complex.

final_content.statement: Let $X$ be a simplicial group. Then $X$ is a Kan complex.

semantic_review_note: Any simplicial group is a Kan complex as an underlying simplicial set, without assuming commutativity.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-surjection-simplicial-abelian-groups-kan}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups
which is termwise surjective. Then $f$ is a Kan fibration of
simplicial sets.

final_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups
which is termwise surjective. Then $f$ is a Kan fibration of
simplicial sets.
hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups
which is termwise surjective.
conclusions:
$f$ is a Kan fibration of
simplicial sets.

semantic_review_note: If f is surjective on each degree as a map of simplicial abelian groups, it meets the horn-lifting criterion for Kan fibrations after forgetting addition; full degreewise surjectivity retained.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups
which is termwise surjective and induces a quasi-isomorphism on
associated chain complexes. Then $f$ is a trivial Kan fibration of
simplicial sets.

final_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homomorphism of simplicial abelian groups

conclusions:
$f$ is a trivial Kan fibration of
simplicial sets.

semantic_review_note: Surjectivity in every simplicial degree and quasi-isomorphism of associated complexes jointly imply f is a trivial Kan fibration; both source antecedents appear.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homotopy-equivalence}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a map of simplicial abelian groups. If $f$ is a
homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets, then $f$ induces a
quasi-isomorphism of associated chain complexes.

final_content.statement:

quasi-isomorphism of associated chain complexes.

homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets,
conclusions:
$f$ induces a
quasi-isomorphism of associated chain complexes.

semantic_review_note: Simplicial homotopy equivalence of an abelian-group map implies quasi-isomorphism of the induced Moore-complex map; only this direction is stated.
